limitations_and_boundaries: Only four datasets were used, all from cancer cell lines.
Datasets are from cancer cell lines, which may have high mutational burden; some foundation models (e.g., Geneformer) excluded such data from training.
Original quality control procedures were not improved; perturbations that did not affect expression of their own target gene were not excluded.
scFoundation was not included in single perturbation benchmark because most required genes were missing from Adamson and Replogle datasets.
CPA was not evaluated in single perturbation benchmark as it is not designed for unseen perturbations.
The benchmark tested only prediction of transcriptome changes after single or double perturbations; other tasks may yield different results.

research_questions.statement: Do deep learning foundation models for single-cell data outperform simple linear baselines in predicting gene expression changes after genetic perturbations?

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: None of the deep learning models was able to consistently outperform the mean prediction or the linear model (Fig. 2a and Extended Data Fig. 8).

claims.statement: None of the deep learning models (GEARS, scGPT, UCE, scBERT, Geneformer) consistently outperformed the mean baseline or the linear model in predicting unseen single perturbation effects.

datasets.name: Adamson et al. K562 CRISPR interference dataset
Replogle et al. K562 CRISPR interference dataset
Replogle et al. RPE1 CRISPR interference dataset

experiments_or_tasks: Prediction of effects for unseen single perturbations on three datasets: Adamson et al. (K562), Replogle et al. (K562 and RPE1). Models compared against mean baseline and linear model baseline. Benchmark repeated twice using GEARS' train-test splitting procedure.

methods.name: Mean baseline
methods.protocol_description: Predicts the mean expression across training perturbations for any unseen perturbation.

methods.name: Linear model (LM)
methods.protocol_description: Represents each read-out gene with a K-dimensional vector (gene embedding G) and each perturbation with an L-dimensional vector (perturbation embedding P). G and P are derived via PCA from training data or from pretrained embeddings. W is found via ridge regression (λ=0.1). Predicts as Y_hat = G W P^T + b, where b is the row mean of training data.

methods.name: GEARS
methods.protocol_description: Deep learning model using Gene Ontology annotations to extrapolate to unseen perturbations, version 0.1.2.

methods.name: scGPT
methods.protocol_description: Single-cell foundation model, parameters and code from perturbation prediction tutorial.

methods.name: UCE (with linear decoder)
methods.protocol_description: Single-cell foundation model, zero-shot, with linear ridge regression decoder.

methods.name: scBERT (with linear decoder)
methods.protocol_description: Fine-tuned on perturbation labels, with linear ridge regression decoder.

methods.name: Geneformer (with linear decoder)
methods.protocol_description: Fine-tuned by predicting perturbation labels, with linear ridge regression decoder.

methods.name: LM with P from Replogle data
methods.protocol_description: Linear model using a perturbation embedding P derived from 10-dimensional PCA on the perturbation means of the Replogle dataset (cross-cell-line pretraining).

methods.name: LM with G from scFoundation
methods.protocol_description: Linear model using gene embedding G extracted from scFoundation's pretrained model weights.

methods.name: LM with G from scGPT
methods.protocol_description: Linear model using gene embedding G extracted from scGPT following their gene regulatory inference tutorial.

methods.name: LM with P from GEARS
methods.protocol_description: Linear model using perturbation embedding P derived from GEARS' Gene Ontology annotations via spectral embedding.

results.metric_name: Number of perturbations included in analysis

provenance.text_excerpt: To evaluate all models on a consistent set of perturbations, we restricted our analysis to those perturbations for which we had predictions from all models (73 perturbations for Adamson, 398 for Replogle K562 and 629 for Replogle RPE1).

results.value_raw_text: To evaluate all models on a consistent set of perturbations, we restricted our analysis to those perturbations for which we had predictions from all models (73 perturbations for Adamson, 398 for Replogle K562 and 629 for Replogle RPE1).

results.metric_name: Relative prediction error vs mean baseline

provenance.text_excerpt: The linear models with the gene embeddings from scFoundation and scGPT outperformed the ‘mean’ baseline, but they did not consistently outperform the linear model using G and P from the training data. The approach that did consistently outperform all other models was a linear model with P pretrained on the Replogle data (using the K562 cell line data as pretraining for the Adamson and RPE1 data and the RPE1 cell line for the K562 data).

results.value_raw_text: The linear models with the gene embeddings from scFoundation and scGPT outperformed the ‘mean’ baseline, but they did not consistently outperform the linear model using G and P from the training data. The approach that did consistently outperform all other models was a linear model with P pretrained on the Replogle data.

provenance.text_excerpt: All models had a prediction error substantially higher than the additive baseline (Fig. 1a,b). None of the models was better than the ‘no change’ baseline.

claims.statement: None of the seven deep learning models (scGPT, scFoundation, UCE, scBERT, Geneformer, GEARS, CPA) outperformed the additive baseline in predicting double perturbation effects; none outperformed the no-change baseline in predicting genetic interactions.

datasets.description: Dataset with 224 perturbations (100 single, 124 double) plus control, with log-transformed RNA-seq expression values for 19,264 genes. Accessed via scFoundation.
datasets.name: Norman et al. K562 CRISPR activation dataset

experiments_or_tasks: Prediction of expression changes after double perturbations using data from Norman et al., with 100 single-gene and 124 double-gene CRISPR activation perturbations in K562 cells. Models were fine-tuned on all 100 single and 62 double perturbations and tested on the remaining 62 double perturbations, repeated across 5 random train-test splits.

methods.name: No change baseline
methods.protocol_description: Predicts for each double perturbation the expression values of the control condition.

methods.name: Additive baseline
methods.protocol_description: Predicts expression for double perturbation of genes A and B as y_A + y_B - y_control, using mean observed expression of single perturbations.

methods.name: scGPT
methods.protocol_description: Single-cell foundation model, fine-tuned using parameters and code from the scGPT tutorial for perturbation prediction.

methods.name: scFoundation
methods.protocol_description: Single-cell foundation model, trained for 5 epochs with fine-tuning time limited to 3 days.

methods.name: UCE (with linear decoder)
methods.protocol_description: Single-cell foundation model used zero-shot; four-layer version. Post-perturbation embedding computed by overwriting perturbed gene rows with ground truth expression. Linear ridge regression decoder fitted on training data to predict gene expression from perturbed embeddings.

methods.name: scBERT (with linear decoder)
methods.protocol_description: Fine-tuned on predicting perturbation labels; post-perturbation embedding by overwriting perturbed gene rows. Linear ridge regression decoder as for UCE.

methods.name: Geneformer (with linear decoder)
methods.protocol_description: Fine-tuned by predicting perturbation labels; used built-in in silico perturbation to compute perturbed embedding. Linear ridge regression decoder.

methods.name: GEARS
methods.protocol_description: Deep learning model for perturbation prediction, used with default parameters version 0.1.2.

methods.name: CPA
methods.protocol_description: Compositional perturbation autoencoder, used with code from tutorial on combinatorial CRISPR perturbations on Norman dataset, version 0.8.8.
